milestones.title: M1 — Desktop foundation
milestones.objective: Stand up the Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript shell with system tray, window lifecycle, local settings persistence, logging, and the base app layout matching the Pi Control design reference.

milestones.title: M2 — Device registry and SSH connectivity
milestones.objective: Let the user register, edit, and remove devices; connect to them over Windows OpenSSH with proper timeout/authentication/host-key error classification; persist devices.json.

milestones.title: M3 — Monitoring engine
milestones.objective: Collect system metrics and Docker container status per device over SSH, build immutable snapshots, and run a bounded-concurrency scheduler with manual and automatic refresh and partial-failure isolation.

milestones.title: M4 — Desktop experience
milestones.objective: Deliver the final dashboard, device detail, services, and settings screens matching the Pi Control design, plus terminal/service launching, deduplicated notifications, and autostart.

workUnits.title: Scaffold Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript project
workUnits.objective: Create the pi-hub Tauri 2 application with a React/TypeScript/Vite frontend and Rust backend matching the suggested repository structure.
scope: Initialize Tauri 2 project with React + TypeScript + Vite template
Set up src-tauri/src layered folders: commands, application, domain, infrastructure, monitoring, platform, storage
Set up frontend src folders: app, components, features, lib, stores, types
Base window configuration (size, title) and tauri.conf.json capabilities scaffolding
Add root README describing how to run the app in dev mode
outOfScope: Do not implement tray, device logic, or SSH yet
acceptanceCriteria: `npm run tauri dev` launches a blank window on Windows
Repository layout matches the structure documented in docs/pi-hub-technical-architecture-specification.md section 27
cargo build and npm run build both succeed

workUnits.title: System tray and window lifecycle
workUnits.objective: Add the Windows system tray icon and menu, and make closing the main window minimize to tray instead of quitting.
scope: Tray icon creation on startup
Tray menu: Open Pi-Hub, Refresh All (stub), Exit
Close button minimizes to tray; Exit terminates the app
Restore/focus main window from tray
outOfScope: Per-device tray shortcuts (added once devices exist in M2/M4)
acceptanceCriteria: Tray icon appears in the Windows notification area on launch
Closing the main window keeps the process running in the tray
Exit from the tray menu terminates the application

workUnits.title: Local settings persistence and logging foundation
workUnits.objective: Implement versioned JSON storage for config.json with atomic writes plus a rotating local log, and expose get_app_settings/save_app_settings commands.
scope: Storage adapter: serialize to temp file, flush, atomic replace, preserve previous file on failure
config.json schema with schemaVersion, refreshIntervalSeconds, startWithWindows, minimizeToTray, notificationsEnabled, theme
get_app_settings / save_app_settings Tauri commands with typed frontend wrappers
Rotating log file under the app data directory with error/warn/info/debug levels, default info
Recovery behavior when config.json is missing or corrupted
acceptanceCriteria: Settings changes survive an application restart
A corrupted config.json does not crash the app; it recovers to defaults and logs a warning
No secrets or private-key content ever appear in logs

workUnits.title: App shell and navigation matching the Pi Control design
workUnits.objective: Build the base React layout (dark theme, 64px icon nav rail, main content area) and lightweight internal routing across Dashboard/Services/Settings, following the Pi Control Claude Design reference.
scope: Design tokens (CSS variables) for the dark theme: background/panel/border/text colors, status colors (healthy/warning/offline)
Nav rail component with Dashboard/Services/Settings icon buttons and active-state highlighting
Lightweight internal router/state for switching between dashboard, device detail, services, device settings, and global settings screens
Empty-state placeholder content for each screen (real content comes in M4)
outOfScope: Real device data, metrics, or Docker data
The per-container 'Update' action shown in the design mockup (Phase 2 scope — do not wire any backend command for it)
acceptanceCriteria: Nav rail navigates between Dashboard, Services, and Settings placeholders
Visual style (colors, spacing, typography) matches the Pi Control Claude Design reference
No arbitrary command execution is exposed to the frontend from this shell

workUnits.title: Device domain model and devices.json repository
workUnits.objective: Define the Device and DeviceService domain models in Rust and TypeScript, and persist them in a versioned devices.json with atomic writes.
scope: Rust Device/DeviceService/DeviceType structs with serde
TypeScript mirror types in src/types
DeviceRepository trait + JSON file implementation reusing the storage adapter from M1
get_devices / get_device Tauri commands
acceptanceCriteria: Devices persist across an application restart
devices.json includes schemaVersion and validates on load
Rust unit tests cover domain validation rules (host, port, username format)

workUnits.title: Device CRUD commands and validation
workUnits.objective: Implement create_device / update_device / delete_device commands with strict input validation for host, port, username, and service URLs.
scope: Validation for hostname/IPv4/IPv6/MagicDNS, SSH port range, Linux username, and http/https-only service URLs
create_device / update_device / delete_device Tauri commands wired to the device repository
Frontend-safe ApplicationError model (code, message, remediation, retryable)
outOfScope: SSH connectivity test itself (next work unit)
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid host/port/username/service URL values are rejected with a clear ApplicationError
Shell metacharacters in any field are rejected
Rust unit tests cover valid and invalid input cases

workUnits.title: SSH adapter and remote command catalogue
workUnits.objective: Implement controlled process execution of the Windows OpenSSH client with a fixed RemoteOperation catalogue (Probe, SystemIdentity, SystemMetrics, DockerContainers) and hard timeouts.
scope: RemoteExecutor trait + Windows OpenSSH process-based implementation using BatchMode=yes and ConnectTimeout
RemoteExecutionResult struct (exit_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms, timed_out)
Connectivity probe using `printf 'PIHUB_OK'`
Error classification: DnsResolutionError, ConnectionTimeout, ConnectionRefused, AuthenticationError, HostKeyError, RemoteCommandError, RemoteCommandTimeout
Arguments passed as separate process args, never string-interpolated
acceptanceCriteria: A fake RemoteExecutor can be substituted in tests to simulate online, offline, timeout, authentication failure, and host-key failure
Host-key errors are never auto-resolved or bypassed
Every remote execution enforces a hard timeout

workUnits.title: Connection testing command and device forms UI
workUnits.objective: Wire test_device_connection into the backend/frontend and build the add/edit/delete device forms styled per the Pi Control device-settings screen.
scope: test_device_connection Tauri command using the SSH adapter's probe operation
Add/Edit/Delete device forms (name, hostname, SSH user, port, description, device type, refresh interval, monitoring/notifications toggles)
Connection status feedback in the UI (online/offline/authentication_error/host_key_error/timeout/unknown)
outOfScope: System metrics or Docker data display (M3/M4)
acceptanceCriteria: Raspberry Pi 2 and Raspberry Pi 5 can be registered, edited, and deleted end-to-end through the UI
Connection test results distinguish authentication failure from host-key failure in the UI
No SSH password is ever requested or stored

workUnits.title: Remote system metrics collection and parsing
workUnits.objective: Collect CPU, memory, disk, temperature, uptime, load average, model, OS, kernel, and architecture in one SSH session using a stable key-value payload, and parse it defensively.
scope: SystemMetrics remote operation reading /proc/stat (CPU delta), /proc/meminfo, /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp, root filesystem disk usage, uname-derived identity fields
PIHUB_* key-value parser: ignore unknown fields, reject invalid numeric values, preserve valid fields, return partial warnings
SystemMetrics domain struct with optional fields for anything that may be unavailable
acceptanceCriteria: Missing/optional fields (e.g. temperature) never fail the whole metrics collection
Malformed key-value lines produce warnings without discarding valid fields
Rust unit tests cover well-formed, partially-malformed, and empty payloads

workUnits.title: Docker discovery and container parsing
workUnits.objective: Detect Docker availability and list containers read-only via `docker ps -a --no-trunc --format '{{json .}}'`, parsing each line independently.
scope: Docker availability check via `command -v docker`
Container listing command and JSON-lines parser producing DockerContainerSummary (name, image, state, statusText, health, ports)
Malformed lines create warnings without discarding valid entries
dockerAvailable=false path when Docker is missing or the SSH user lacks permission, without marking the device offline
outOfScope: Any container start/stop/restart/exec (explicitly out of MVP scope)
acceptanceCriteria: A device with Docker unavailable still reports online with valid system metrics
A Docker permission error is classified as DockerPermissionError and does not fail the whole device refresh
Rust unit tests cover well-formed, malformed, and empty docker ps output

workUnits.title: Monitoring scheduler, snapshots, and bounded concurrency
workUnits.objective: Build the refresh lifecycle: probe, collect metrics, collect Docker data, assemble an immutable DeviceSnapshot, and run it on a scheduler with bounded concurrency and manual/automatic refresh.
scope: DeviceSnapshot domain struct (connectionStatus, capturedAt, durationMs, metrics, dockerAvailable, containers, warnings, error)
Scheduler with configurable interval (default 60s, 15-3600s range), max 4 concurrent refreshes, one active refresh per device
refresh_device / refresh_all_devices / get_latest_snapshot Tauri commands
Backend events: device://snapshot-updated, device://status-changed, container://status-changed, monitoring://refresh-started, monitoring://refresh-completed
state.json persistence of last-known snapshots (non-authoritative; app must work if deleted)
acceptanceCriteria: A failing/offline device does not stop the scheduler or block other devices' refreshes
Manual refresh and automatic refresh both work without freezing the UI
Stale snapshots remain visible with an explicit stale marker and last-refresh timestamp after a failed refresh
Deleting state.json does not prevent the app from starting

workUnits.title: Status-transition detection and notification decisions
workUnits.objective: Compare consecutive snapshots to detect device and container state transitions and decide when a notification should fire, with deduplication persisted across restarts.
scope: Device transition rules: online<->offline, online->authentication_error, online->host_key_error
Container transition rules: running->exited/stopped/restarting/unhealthy (skip containers already stopped when first discovered)
Deduplication key: deviceId + resourceId + previousState + currentState, persisted in state.json
NotificationService trait producing notification-ready events (actual OS notification dispatch happens in M4)
acceptanceCriteria: Repeated refreshes with an unchanged state never produce duplicate notification events
A container already stopped at first discovery does not trigger a notification
Rust unit tests cover each transition rule and the dedup key

workUnits.title: Dashboard screen
workUnits.objective: Implement the dashboard device-card grid wired to live snapshot events, matching the Pi Control design reference.
scope: Device card: status dot with pulse animation, name, model badge, hostname, offline banner, CPU/MEM/DISK/TEMP mini bars with color thresholds, uptime, container count, last refresh
Refresh All button and per-card Refresh button wired to refresh_all_devices / refresh_device
Terminal and Services quick actions per card
Loading, empty, and stale-data states
outOfScope: The per-container 'Update' action from the design mockup (Phase 2 — not in MVP command boundary)
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard shows every registered device with live status and metrics from device://snapshot-updated events
Stale data is visibly marked and includes a refresh timestamp
Refreshing all devices does not block the UI

workUnits.title: Device detail screen
workUnits.objective: Implement the device detail view: general information, system metrics, recent activity, Docker container table, and registered services, matching the design reference.
scope: General information panel (hostname, IP, model, SSH user)
System metrics panel with CPU/MEM/DISK/TEMP bars and uptime/container/last-refresh summary line
Docker container table (name, status, image, uptime, health, port) with empty/offline states
Registered services list for the device
Recent activity feed sourced from notification/transition history
acceptanceCriteria: Device detail view reflects the latest snapshot for the selected device
A Docker permission or unavailability error shows a clear message without hiding valid system metrics
Navigating back returns to the dashboard preserving its state

workUnits.title: Services grid and settings screens
workUnits.objective: Implement the global services grid (with device filter), per-device settings panel, and global settings panel matching the design reference.
scope: Services grid: tiles with icon/name/URL, device filter chip, empty state
Device settings: name/hostname/SSH user/description/refresh interval form, notification toggles, registered services list
Global settings: theme (dark/light/system), start-with-Windows toggle, default refresh interval, global notification toggle, About panel
outOfScope: Backend theme persistence beyond what M1's settings storage already provides
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting a service opens it in the default browser via open_device_service, restricted to http/https
Device and global settings changes persist via save_app_settings / update_device and survive a restart
Settings screens visually match the Pi Control design reference

workUnits.title: Terminal launcher, service launcher, and tray shortcuts
workUnits.objective: Implement open_device_terminal (Windows Terminal via wt.exe ssh) and open_device_service (default browser), and add per-device shortcuts to the tray menu.
scope: open_device_terminal command launching wt.exe ssh <user>@<host> (or -p <port>) with arguments passed separately
open_device_service command validating and opening http/https URLs in the default browser
Tray menu extended with per-device Open Terminal / Open Service shortcuts
Terminal-launch failure handling and remediation messaging
outOfScope: Embedded terminal UI (explicitly out of MVP scope)
acceptanceCriteria: SSH terminal sessions open in Windows Terminal for both Raspberry Pis
Home Assistant and Personal Finance services open in the default browser
No command string is ever built via interpolation; all arguments are passed separately to the process API

workUnits.title: Windows notification dispatch and notification settings
workUnits.objective: Dispatch native Windows notifications from the M3 notification decisions, with global and per-device enable/disable controls wired into settings.
scope: Native notification dispatch via the Tauri notification plugin for device/container transitions and repeated auth/host-key failures
Global notification toggle and per-device notification toggle wired to settings
End-to-end wiring from monitoring::notifications decisions to the platform dispatch
outOfScope: Per-event-type notification controls (future scope per spec)
acceptanceCriteria: A device going offline then online produces exactly one offline and one online notification, not a stream of duplicates
Disabling notifications globally or for a specific device suppresses dispatch accordingly
MVP acceptance criteria 12 (deduplicated transition notifications) is demonstrably met

workUnits.title: Windows autostart preference
workUnits.objective: Wire the official Tauri autostart plugin to the start-with-Windows setting, default disabled.
scope: set_autostart / get_autostart_status Tauri commands using the Tauri autostart plugin
Global settings toggle wired to autostart, default disabled until explicitly enabled
acceptanceCriteria: Enabling the setting registers Pi-Hub to launch minimized at Windows sign-in
Disabling it removes the registration
Default state after first install is disabled

checkpoints.summary: Implemented create_device/update_device/delete_device with strict validation, via a new application::device_service layer (commands -> application -> domain -> storage). Extended Device::validate() to also validate each service's name and URL (http/https only). create_device generates a UUID id and RFC3339 timestamps; update_device preserves id/created_at while bumping updated_at and 404s on an unknown id; delete_device 404s if nothing was removed; all three validate before ever touching disk, so invalid input never persists or corrupts the existing device list. 12 new Rust unit tests, 43 total passing.
completed: domain/device.rs: Device::validate() now also validates each registered service's name (non-empty) and url (must parse and use http or https; rejects javascript:, file:, data:, and malformed URLs).
application/device_service.rs: DeviceInput (editable fields only, no client-settable id/createdAt/updatedAt) + create_device/update_device/delete_device.
create_device: generates a UUID v4 id and matching RFC3339 created_at/updated_at (via chrono), validates, then persists.
update_device: looks up the existing device by id (NotFound if missing), preserves id and created_at, bumps updated_at, validates, then persists; a rejected update never touches the stored list.
delete_device: removes by id, NotFound if nothing was removed.

commands/devices.rs: create_device/update_device/delete_device Tauri commands, mapping DeviceServiceError to the existing ApplicationError (ValidationError/NotFoundError/StorageError); registered in lib.rs.
src/types/device.ts + src/lib/tauri/devices.ts: added DeviceInput type and createDevice/updateDevice/deleteDevice wrappers.
Added uuid, chrono, and url as direct Cargo dependencies.
12 new Rust unit tests (5 domain service-URL/name validation, 7 application-layer create/update/delete including rejected-input-doesn't-persist cases), for 43 total.
Verified cargo test (43/43), cargo build, npm run build, and npm run lint all pass.

checkpoints.summary: Implemented the SSH adapter: a RemoteExecutor trait backed by OpenSshExecutor (controlled process execution of Windows OpenSSH, BatchMode=yes, ConnectTimeout, args passed separately never string-interpolated), a hard-timeout-enforcing process primitive verified against real OS processes, an SshError classification enum mapping onto DeviceConnectionStatus, the RemoteOperation catalogue (Probe wired up now; SystemIdentity/SystemMetrics/DockerContainers reserved for M3), and a FakeRemoteExecutor test double covering all five required simulation scenarios. 30 new Rust unit tests, 64 total passing; also manually cross-checked the classification heuristics against this machine's real ssh.exe output.
completed: domain/connection_status.rs: DeviceConnectionStatus enum matching spec section 9.3.
infrastructure/ssh/process.rs: run_with_timeout() -- SSH-agnostic hard-timeout enforcement via try_wait() polling + kill on deadline, unit-tested against real cmd/ping processes (not just mocked).
infrastructure/ssh/operation.rs: RemoteOperation catalogue (Probe, SystemIdentity, SystemMetrics, DockerContainers); only Probe has a command body now.

infrastructure/ssh/error.rs: SshError (DnsResolutionError/ConnectionRefused/ConnectionTimeout/AuthenticationError/HostKeyError/RemoteCommandError/RemoteCommandTimeout/Spawn) + to_connection_status() mapping; HostKeyError always maps to HostKeyError, never auto-resolved.

infrastructure/ssh/openssh.rs: OpenSshExecutor building `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=<n> -p <port> <user>@<host> <command>` with every arg passed separately; classify_outcome() interprets exit code 255 + stderr text into the right SshError.
infrastructure/ssh/executor.rs: RemoteExecutor trait, RemoteExecutionResult/SshTarget types, default probe() method.
infrastructure/ssh/fake.rs (test-only): FakeRemoteExecutor with online/offline/timeout/authentication_error/host_key_error constructors for this and future (M3) tests.

Verified with cargo test (64/64), cargo build, npm run build, npm run lint, and a live smoke test that confirmed the Dashboard empty state and the full Add Device form render correctly; full interactive click-through wasn't completed live because the desktop's foreground focus kept getting reclaimed by another active application during the session and repeatedly forcing it felt like the wrong call on someone's active desktop -- that gap is covered by existing WU006/WU007 unit tests exercising the same command logic end-to-end.

infrastructure/ssh/executor.rs: probe() now routes through RemoteOperation::Probe.command() instead of a raw constant.

commands/devices.rs: async test_device_connection -- validates host/port/username, runs the probe via tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking (probe can take up to 5s and must not block the async runtime), returns ConnectionTestResult{status, message} for every outcome including failures.

checkpoints.summary: Implemented the SystemMetrics remote operation (a single POSIX sh script collecting CPU/memory/disk/temperature/load/uptime/identity in one SSH round trip, syntax-checked with both sh -n and dash -n) and a defensive PIHUB_* key-value parser that never fails on a missing or invalid individual field. 18 new Rust unit tests, 82 total passing.
completed: domain/system_metrics.rs: SystemMetrics with every field Option<_>, matching this work unit's explicit scope of optional fields for anything that may be unavailable.

infrastructure/ssh/operation.rs: SYSTEM_METRICS_COMMAND, a single POSIX sh script collecting CPU usage (two-sample /proc/stat delta with a bounded 0.3s sleep), memory (/proc/meminfo), root-disk usage (df -Pk /), temperature (primary thermal zone, optional), load average (/proc/loadavg), uptime (/proc/uptime), and identity fields (hostname/model/OS/kernel/arch) folded into the same session rather than a separate SystemIdentity round trip.
infrastructure/parsers/key_value.rs: parse_key_value_payload() -- generic PIHUB_KEY=value parser; non-PIHUB_ or malformed lines produce a warning instead of aborting.

infrastructure/parsers/metrics.rs: parse_system_metrics() rejects invalid numeric values (with a warning) while preserving every other valid field; memory/disk used-bytes are derived from total-available and only set when available <= total (guards against a nonsensical negative value). collect_system_metrics() wires a RemoteExecutor + SshTarget to the fixed command and the parser.
Marked both new modules #[allow(dead_code, unused_imports)] since nothing calls into them yet -- the M3 scheduler work unit wires them up -- following the WU007 precedent.

18 new Rust unit tests: 6 for the generic key-value parser, 12 for system-metrics parsing (full payload, empty payload, missing-optional-field survival, invalid-numeric survival, mixed malformed/unrecognized lines, memory-used derivation incl. the available>total guard, temperature conversion, and collect_system_metrics integration via FakeRemoteExecutor for both success and connection failure).
Verified cargo test (82/82), cargo build (no warnings), and npm run build all pass.
Syntax-checked the remote script with both `sh -n` and `dash -n` (dash closely matches Raspberry Pi OS's default /bin/sh) and hand-verified the CPU-delta arithmetic against a worked example.

checkpoints.summary: Implemented Docker availability detection and read-only container listing. The remote script always exits 0 when Docker isn't installed (reported via a PIHUB_DOCKER_AVAILABLE marker, never a command failure); when Docker is available, docker ps's own exit code/stderr propagate naturally, which required enriching SshError::RemoteCommandError with stderr so a permission-denied failure can be distinguished from any other command error. Both Unavailable and PermissionDenied are normal Ok outcomes at the collect_docker_containers layer, never surfaced as SshError. 17 new Rust unit tests, 99 total passing.
completed: infrastructure/ssh/operation.rs: DOCKER_CONTAINERS_COMMAND -- checks `command -v docker`, prints PIHUB_DOCKER_AVAILABLE=0/1, then runs `docker ps -a --no-trunc --format '{{json .}}'` as the script's final command so its exit status/stderr propagate through the existing error path.
infrastructure/ssh/error.rs: enriched SshError::RemoteCommandError with stderr (was exit_code only); updated Display impl and existing WU007 tests.
domain/docker_container.rs: DockerContainerState/DockerHealthStatus/DockerPortBinding/DockerContainerSummary matching spec section 9.5.

infrastructure/parsers/docker.rs: parse_docker_containers() parses docker ps JSON lines independently (malformed lines warn and are skipped, valid ones kept); state strings map to DockerContainerState with unrecognized -> Unknown; health is derived from the Status text since docker ps has no dedicated health field; ports parsed from Docker's host->container/protocol string format, tolerating unpublished ports and multiple bindings.
collect_docker_containers(): runs the fixed operation and classifies into DockerCollectionResult::{Available, Unavailable, PermissionDenied} -- the latter two are normal Ok outcomes, never SshError.
Marked the new domain/parser code #[allow(dead_code)] since nothing calls it yet -- the M3 scheduler wires it up -- following the WU007/WU009 precedent.

17 new Rust unit tests: well-formed/malformed/empty docker ps payloads, port parsing edge cases, health/state derivation, the availability marker, and collect_docker_containers integration via FakeRemoteExecutor across all five outcome types.

checkpoints.summary: Built the full refresh lifecycle: DeviceSnapshot domain struct, state.json persistence, a pure per-device refresh function that preserves last-known data on failure (stale marking), a RefreshCoordinator enforcing max-4-concurrent and one-active-refresh-per-device, a 5s background tick loop driving automatic refresh via managed Tauri state (no unsafe), refresh_device/refresh_all_devices/get_latest_snapshot commands, and the five backend events. 24 new Rust unit tests including a real #[tokio::test] proving the concurrency bound, 123 total passing. Live smoke test confirmed the automatic scheduler end-to-end via state.json, with no UI interaction needed.
completed: domain/snapshot.rs: DeviceSnapshot with stale + lastSuccessfulRefresh fields; failed refreshes carry forward previous metrics/dockerAvailable/containers rather than clearing them.

storage/snapshot_repository.rs: JsonSnapshotRepository for state.json, same atomic-write/corrupted-file-quarantine pattern as config/device repositories; verified the app stays functional after state.json is deleted mid-session.

monitoring/refresh.rs: refresh_device_sync() -- pure, synchronous per-device refresh logic; a failed probe classifies status and stops (stale=true, prior data preserved); a successful probe collects metrics+Docker independently so a Docker failure becomes a warning, not a device failure.

monitoring/concurrency.rs: RefreshCoordinator (Semaphore for max-4-concurrent + in-progress set for one-per-device dedup), with a real #[tokio::test] proving the semaphore actually blocks a 3rd permit under max_concurrent=2 and releases correctly.
monitoring/container_diff.rs: detect_container_changes() -- structural diff powering container://status-changed; deliberately excludes notification-worthiness rules (WU012's job).
monitoring/scheduling.rs: is_due() comparing capturedAt against the device's own interval or the global default.

monitoring/scheduler.rs: refresh_one/refresh_all + a 5s background tick loop started from setup(); looks up RefreshCoordinator via Tauri's managed state (app.state::<T>()) rather than passing borrowed references into spawned tasks, avoiding any unsafe/raw-pointer lifetime workaround. Emits monitoring://refresh-started/-completed, device://snapshot-updated, device://status-changed (only on actual change), container://status-changed (only when non-empty).
commands/monitoring.rs: refresh_device/refresh_all_devices (async, SSH work runs off the async runtime's blocking pool) / get_latest_snapshot.
infrastructure/ssh/error.rs: added SshError::code() mapping to the spec error taxonomy, replacing an ad hoc Debug-string-split.
error.rs: ApplicationError now derives Clone/PartialEq/Deserialize so it round-trips through persisted state.json.
Added tokio (rt/sync/time/macros) as a direct dependency.
src/types/snapshot.ts + src/lib/tauri/monitoring.ts: TypeScript mirror types and command wrappers.
24 new Rust unit tests, 123 total passing. Verified cargo test, cargo build (no warnings), npm run build.

Live smoke test: seeded a device pointing at a closed local port directly into devices.json, launched the app with zero UI interaction, and confirmed via state.json that the background tick loop detected it was due, ran a real ssh.exe probe (genuine ConnectionRefused), classified it Offline, and persisted a snapshot with stale=true -- proving the automatic-refresh path end-to-end without real Pi hardware.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A failing/offline device does not stop the scheduler or block other devices' refreshes
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: refresh_all spawns one task per device and swallows individual failures when collecting results ("if let Ok(Ok(snapshot))"); tick() spawns each due device's refresh independently. failed_probe_marks_stale_and_carries_forward_previous_data and friends confirm a single device's failure produces a valid (Offline/stale) snapshot rather than propagating an error that would abort other work.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Manual refresh and automatic refresh both work without freezing the UI
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: refresh_device/refresh_all_devices are async Tauri commands that run the blocking SSH work via spawn_blocking; the automatic path uses the same refresh_one() function via a background tokio task started at setup(), independently confirmed live via the state.json smoke test.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Stale snapshots remain visible with an explicit stale marker and last-refresh timestamp after a failed refresh
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: DeviceSnapshot.stale + capturedAt are always populated; failed_probe_marks_stale_and_carries_forward_previous_data test and the live smoke test's actual state.json output (stale: true, capturedAt populated) both confirm this.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Deleting state.json does not prevent the app from starting
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: app_remains_functional_after_state_json_is_deleted test explicitly deletes the file mid-session and confirms subsequent reads/writes still work; load_all() unconditionally recovers to an empty map on a missing file.
